features.name: Blood Potency
features.entriesHtml:
You are fueled by blood, represented by Blood Points. Your Kindred level determines the number of points you have, as shown in the Blood Points column of the Kindred Features table. You can expend Blood Points in the following ways:

Heal Wounds.

As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can expend 1 Blood Point to regain Hit Points|XPHB equal to 1d10 plus your Kindred level.

Hunger Sated.

If you fail a D20 Test|XPHB that is affected by your Beast feature, you can expend 1 Blood Point to ignore the effects of The Beast|Kindred|BoundByBlood|1||Hunger.

Vitae Powers.

There are Kindred feats|feats|category=kf and subclass features fueled by expending Blood Points.

features.name: Feed
features.entriesHtml:
You feed on the blood of other creatures. This is most often accomplished through your sharp fangs. As an action, you can feed on another creature within 5 feet of yourself if the target is willing, Charmed by you, or has the Incapacitated, Grappled, Paralyzed, Restrained, Stunned, or Unconscious condition. You can feed only once per turn.

When you feed, roll up to your maximum Feed Dice plus your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1). The creature takes Necrotic damage equal to the roll's total. This damage only reduces the creature's Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum by an amount equal to the roll's total. The number of Feed Dice increases as you gain Kindred levels, as shown in the Feed Dice column of the Kindred Features table. If you roll a 6 on a d6 on a Feed Die, you can regain 1 expended Blood Point. If a creature's Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum is reduced to 0, you can regain 1 expended Blood Point.

Feeding from the Willing.

If you feed on a willing creature or a creature Charmed by you, it can spend 1 Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die. It rolls the Hit Point Dice|XPHB|Hit Point Die and reduces its Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum by the amount rolled, and you can regain 1 expended Blood Point. Feeding in this way doesn't end the Charmed condition.

Hit Die Deficit.

If a creature has no remaining Hit Point Dice|XPHB, the creature takes Necrotic damage equal to a roll of your Feed Dice plus your Constitution modifier, and the creature's Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point maximum is reduced by an amount equal to the roll's total.

Maximum Successful Feedings.

A creature can provide a number of Blood Points based on its size. A Small creature provides 1 Blood Point, a Medium provides 3, a Large provides 5, a Huge provides 7, and a Gargantuan provides 10. A creature regains all lost Blood Points when it finishes a Long Rest|XPHB.

Creature Susceptible to Feed.

You can feed on any creature with blood or other life-giving fluid. Aberrations, Beasts, Dragons, Fey, Giants, Monstrosities, and Humanoids are the most common targets. Constructs, Elementals, Oozes, and Plants usually don't have blood. Work with your GM to determine the types of creatures you can feed on.

The Blood Bond.

A mysterious power in the blood of Kindred causes creatures to become Blood Bound to that Kindred when:

  • They drink from the same Kindred at least three times within one year.
  • At least one Long Rest|XPHB occurs between each of the three drinks.

While Blood Bound to a Kindred, a creature is considered Charmed by that Kindred and has Advantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid being Charmed or Frightened by other creatures. This is in addition to the effects from the Kindred Vitae consumable.

A Blood Bond can be suppressed for 1 minute if the creature succeeds on a DC 25 Charisma saving throw. The bond is only permanently removed if the creature doesn't drink from that Kindred again for a year, or if the Kindred in question is killed.

features.name: Kindred Biology
features.entriesHtml:
You are a specific kind of vampire known as a Kindred, which brings physical benefits and drawbacks.

Awaken.

You don't regain expended Blood Points when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB. To gain the benefits of a Long Rest|XPHB, you must have at least 1 Blood Point in your pool or you only gain the benefits of a Short Rest|XPHB.

Darkvision.

You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

Sanguivore.

You can't eat food or drink. If you consume more than a nibble or sip, you have the Poisoned condition that ends once you expel what you consumed. While Poisoned in this way, you must succeed on a Constitution saving throw every 10 minutes to avoid having the Incapacitated condition, which lasts for 1 minute as you vomit up what you've consumed. The initial DC of this saving throw is 10, and it increases by 5 with each successive save.

Instead, you must consume a number of Blood Points per day equal to the number of pounds of food a creature your size normally requires per day (usually, 1 per day for Small and Medium creatures). You can expend 1 Blood Point to automatically succeed on the DC 10 Constitution saving throw to avoid gaining 1 level of Exhaustion from Malnutrition.

Expending Blood Points to activate your Kindred features or Kindred Feats does not count towards the Blood Points you need to expend for sustenance.

Sunlight Vulnerability.

You take 5 Radiant damage if you start your turn in sunlight.

Supernatural Spellcasting.

Charisma is your spellcasting ability for spells from your Kindred subclass and Kindred feats, your spells require no Verbal or Somatic components, and they require no Material components unless they are consumed by the spell or have a cost specified in it; taking damage can't break your Concentration.

Torpor.

If your Exhaustion level is 6, you aren't killed. Instead, you drop to 1 Hit Points|XPHB|Hit Point, become Unconscious, and can't remove the condition until you have expended a number of Blood Points equal to your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus over any length of time. Another creature can feed you while you are Unconscious to recover Blood Points, but the details of how that occurs is left for you and your GM to determine.

Undead.

You have the Undead (Kindred) creature type in addition to your normal creature type. You don't age.

Vampiric Resilience.

You automatically succeed on Death Saving Throw|XPHB|Death Saving Throws. Being reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB by Fire or Radiant damage, or being beheaded kills you outright.

Vampiric Vulnerabilities.

You have Vulnerability|XPHB to Fire and Radiant damage.

Wooden Stake Through the Heart.

When you are attacked with a wooden weapon that deals Piercing damage and you are reduced to 0 Hit Points|XPHB or the attack roll is a Critical Hit|XPHB, you are staked through the heart and have the Paralyzed condition until the weapon is removed.

features.name: The Beast
features.entriesHtml:
You have a terrible Beast within that can only be sated with blood. As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can use this Beast's predatory instincts to sharpen your senses and abilities. Until the start of your next turn, you have Advantage|XPHB on D20 Test|XPHB|D20 Tests you make.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Short Rest|XPHB|Short or Long Rest|XPHB.

Hunger.

If a D20 Test|XPHB benefiting from your Beast feature fails, you go into a bloodlusted, hunger-driven state. This bloodlusted state ends after 1 minute or after you have successfully used your Feed feature, whichever comes first.

While bloodlusted, you regard the creature nearest to you that you can see or hear and that you can feed on as your prey. If there are multiple possible creatures, choose one at random. On each of your turns, you must move as close to the creature as possible and take the Attack action to make an Unarmed Strike|XPHB to grapple the target. If you're unable to get close enough to the creature to grapple it, your turn ends after you've used up all your available movement. If the creature dies or can no longer be seen or heard by you, the next nearest creature that you can see or hear and that you can feed on becomes your new target. If the target is in range and has the Grappled condition at the start of your turn, you use your action to feed on it.

features.name: Depth of Feelings
features.entriesHtml:
You can see aspects of the world that others can't, including emotions. You gain the following benefits.

Aura Sight.

As a Magic action, you can expend 2 Blood Points to see a creature's aura for 1 minute. You can ask the GM up to two questions that can be answered with yes or no. You must ask your questions before the effect ends. You receive a correct answer for each question. The following are example questions.

  • Is the creature's creature type X? (Where X is a creature type specified by the player character, such as Monstrosity or Undead)
  • Can the creature cast spells?
  • Is the creature Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile toward me?
  • Does the creature believe what it is saying?

The GM has final say as to whether the question can be answered, but the answers must be truthful.

Entrancement.

You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the Calm Emotions, Charm Monster, or Charm Person spell.

features.entriesHtml:
You have mastered what it means to be one of the greatest vampiric artisans, which defines you as much as you define it. Choose two of the following benefits.

Flicker.

As a Bonus Action|XPHB, you can expend 3 Blood Points to dance between the beats of a mortal's heart. Until the start of your next turn, you have a +3 bonus to AC, your Speed|XPHB is doubled, your movement doesn't provoke Opportunity Attack, and you have Advantage|XPHB on attack rolls.

Clairvoyance.

You can expend 2 Blood Points to cast the Clairvoyance or Scrying spell. When you cast the spell in this way, the sensor can't be perceived.

Open Mind.

You can use a Magic action to expend 1 Blood point to choose any number of creatures you know within 5 miles of yourself or any number of creatures you can see within 120 feet of yourself. You and the chosen creatures can communicate telepathically with each other while the creatures and you are within 5 miles of each other for 8 hours. You and the targets can instantly share words, images, sounds, and other sensory messages with each other through the link, and the targets recognize you as the creature they are communicating with. This effect enables creatures to understand the meaning of your words and any sensory messages you send to them.

Star Magnetism.

You can expend 3 Blood Points to cast the Mass Suggestion spell. When you cast the spell in this way, you can target any creature you can communicate with, you don't need line of sight, the range becomes 1 mile, and you can modify it so that it doesn't require Concentration.

Befuddle.

You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the Hypnotic Pattern spell. When you cast the spell in this way, a creature with an Intelligence of 3 or lower automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the spell while a creature with an Intelligence of 4 or higher has Disadvantage|XPHB on the saving throw.

Entrance.

As a Magic action, make a Charisma (Persuasion) check and expend 2 Blood Points to choose a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to the result of your Persuasion check. On a failed save, the creature has the Stunned condition until the end of your next turn. At the end of each of the Stunned creature's turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. A creature with an Intelligence of 3 or lower automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the effect.

Persuade.

You can expend 1 Blood Point to cast the Charm Monster spell.

Terrify.

The target must make a Wisdom saving throw with a DC equal to the result of your Intimidation check. On a failed save, the creature has the Frightened condition for 1 minute. At the end of each of the Frightened creature's turns, the creature repeats the save, ending the effect on itself on a success. features.name: Lordly Power
features.entriesHtml:
Your will over others becomes ironclad and staggeringly powerful. You gain the following benefits.

Imposing Aura.

When a creature within 15 feet of you targets you with an attack roll or a damaging spell, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus) or either choose a new target or lose the attack or spell. On a successful save, the target isn't affected, and it's immune to Imposing Aura for 24 hours.

Penetrating Dominance.

Creatures you can see within 60 feet of yourself have Disadvantage|XPHB on saving throws to avoid or end the Charmed condition.

Summon.

As a Magic action, you can expend 3 Blood Points to urge a Beast, Humanoid, or Undead you have touched and is on the same plane of existence as you to make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 8 plus your Charisma modifier and Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus). On a failed save, the creature is compelled to come to you. The creature must use as much of its movement as possible to move in your direction on its turns, taking the safest route, and stopping only to eat and rest. A compelled creature repeats the save at the end of each day at dusk, ending the effect on itself on a success. You know if the compulsion ends early. You can't have more than one creature under this effect at a time. If you use this feature again, the effect on another creature ends.

When the creature appears, it is under no compulsion to behave a particular way. You can ask it to perform a service in exchange for payment, but it isn't obliged to do so. The requested task could range from simple (fly us across the chasm, or help us fight a battle) to complex (spy on our enemies, or protect us during our foray into the dungeon). You must be able to communicate with the creature to bargain for its services. Payment can take a variety of forms.

The GM can adjust these payments based on the circumstances under which you called upon it. If the task is aligned with the creature's ethos, the payment might be halved or even waived. Nonhazardous tasks typically require only half the payment, while especially dangerous tasks might require a greater gift. Creatures rarely accept tasks that seem suicidal.

A Remove Curse, Greater Restoration, or Wish spell ends this effect.
